cards.text: It's the second year of Darius, king of Persia, on the first day of the sixth month. The word of the LORD comes through Haggai the prophet to two leaders: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. The LORD of Hosts starts by repeating what these people have been saying about rebuilding the house of the LORD.

cards.question: What are the people saying about rebuilding the house of the LORD?

answers.text: The time has not yet come
The work is too hard for us
We have no stones to build with

cards.text: Not yet. Friend, that's the snooze button talking, and some of us hit that thing so many times the alarm clock files a COMPLAINT. Then the word of the LORD comes through Haggai again, and this time it's a question.

cards.question: The people say it's not time to rebuild the LORD's house. What does God's question through Haggai point to?

answers.text: Living in paneled houses while His house lies in ruins
Guarding their own walls while His gates stand open
Buying new fields while His priests go without

cards.text: Living in paneled houses while the LORD's house lies in ruins is like me polishing my gold base till it GLOWS while the bakery oven sits there in PIECES. Now the LORD of Hosts says, 'Consider carefully your ways.'

cards.question: God tells the people they have planted much and harvested much.

cards.text: Planted much, harvested LITTLE, and God keeps going: they eat but never have enough, and they drink but never have their fill.

cards.question: God says that when the people put on clothes, they finally get warm.

cards.text: Their clothes never get them warm either, and their paychecks have it rough too. God says, 'You earn wages to put into a bag pierced through.'

cards.question: God says the people put their wages into a bag pierced through. What's the picture?

answers.text: Their money keeps slipping away from them
Thieves keep breaking in and taking their money
They hide their money away and forget about it

cards.text: You know this one, friend: payday hits, and two days later you're staring at your account like, WHERE did it GO? Then God says it again, same words: 'Consider carefully your ways.'
Then the LORD of Hosts gets specific: 'Go up into the hills, bring down lumber, and build the house…'

cards.question: Why does God tell the people to build His house?

answers.text: So He may take pleasure in it and be glorified
So the priests can live in it and be safe
So the governor can rule from it in peace

cards.text: Then God says, 'You expected much, but behold, it amounted to little.' And He tells them what happened to what they did bring home.

cards.question: God says He Himself blew away what the people brought home.

cards.text: God asks, 'Why?' and answers it Himself: His house still lies in ruins, while each of them is busy with his own house. Busy, busy, BUSY, friend, just not on the LORD's house.

cards.question: God says the heavens have withheld their dew on account of the people.
The earth has withheld its crops too. The LORD says He has summoned a ___ on the fields and on the mountains.
God says the drought He has summoned spares the animals.

cards.text: That drought reaches the grain, the new wine, the oil, whatever the ground yields, and all the labor of their hands. We'll let that cool on the rack for now, friend, because this story isn't over.
